title.en: Will It Fit? The Memory Math for Running LLMs Locally

description.en: 2026's small-model wave — Phi-4-mini, Gemma 4, Mistral Small — put real LLMs on laptops. Learn the one calculation that tells you which model fits in your RAM, and why quantization changes everything.

story_variants.en:
## The Question Every Local-AI Builder Asks First

Vaathiyaar taps the RAM sticker on a laptop. "Before you download a single model in 2026, you answer one question: **will it fit?** Get it wrong and your machine swaps to disk and crawls. Get it right and a 12-billion-parameter model like Gemma 4 hums along on a 16 GB laptop."

The 2026 small-model wave — **Phi-4-mini** (3.8B), **Gemma 4** (12B), **Mistral Small 3.2** (24B) — is only useful if you can predict its footprint. And the whole game is a little arithmetic.

### Weights Are Just Numbers, and Numbers Have a Size

A model's parameters are floating-point numbers. Their memory cost is simply:

> **bytes = number_of_parameters x bytes_per_parameter**

At full precision each weight is a 16-bit float — **2 bytes**. So a 7B model in bf16 is `7e9 x 2 = 14 GB` before you've done anything else.

### Quantization: The Trick That Made Local LLMs Real

**Quantization** stores each weight in fewer bits — 8-bit (1 byte), 4-bit (0.5 bytes), even lower — trading a little accuracy for a lot of RAM. That 14 GB model at 4-bit becomes `7e9 x 0.5 = 3.5 GB`. Suddenly it fits on a phone.

| Precision | Bits/weight | Bytes/weight | 7B model |
|---|---|---|---|
| fp32 | 32 | 4 | 28 GB |
| bf16 | 16 | 2 | 14 GB |
| int8 | 8 | 1 | 7 GB |
| int4 | 4 | 0.5 | 3.5 GB |

### Don't Forget the Overhead

Weights aren't the only tenant in RAM. The **KV cache** (attention's memory of the conversation), activations, and framework overhead add on top — a common rule of thumb is to reserve **~20% headroom**. So a model whose weights are 3.5 GB really wants ~4.2 GB free.

> **The builder's rule:** `RAM needed = params x (bits / 8) x 1.2`. Memorize it. It is the difference between "runs beautifully" and "why is my fan screaming?"

Today you'll implement exactly that calculation — the first tool every local-AI engineer writes.

explanation.en: 8 bits to a byte: int4 -> 0.5 bytes, bf16 -> 2 bytes
The dominant cost: one number per parameter
Reserve ~20% for KV cache, activations and framework overhead
Bytes -> gigabytes so you can compare against your RAM sticker
